intro: A New Orleans Mardi Gras Indian group, played as funk.
story: 79rs Gang is a New Orleans group in the Mardi Gras Indian tradition, led by Big Chiefs Romeo Bougere and Jermaine Bossier, who play it as funk, with drums and chants. Expect the Unexpected came out in 2020. They played Pickathon in 2022, and into 2025 they kept playing Tipitina's, the New Orleans club, on Mardi Gras weekend.
sets: Sat Aug 6, 6 pm, Grove · Sun Aug 7, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn

intro: Two New York rappers, billy woods and E L U C I D, as one duo.
story: Armand Hammer is billy woods and E L U C I D, two New York rappers who have made records together on Backwoodz Studioz since 2013. Shrines came out in 2020 and Haram in 2021. They played Pickathon in 2022, a Thursday late night in the Galaxy Barn, in a year when each of them also put out a solo record, Aethiopes and I Told Bessie. We Buy Diabetic Test Strips, on Backwoodz and Fat Possum in 2023, made nineteen year-end lists. Mercury, a record with the Alchemist, followed in 2025, and in November 2026 they surprise-released their eighth album, Snakes & Ladders.
sets: Thu Aug 4, 11 pm, Galaxy Barn · Fri Aug 5, 10 pm

intro: A Los Angeles trio of synthesizers and post-punk.
story: Automatic is a Los Angeles trio that plays synth-driven post-punk, on Stones Throw Records. Signal came out in 2019, and Excess in 2022, the year they played Pickathon; Mojo heard their sparse minimalism as edgy drive. Is It Now?, their third album, arrived in July 2025, they toured internationally through late 2026, and they came back to the farm in 2026.
sets: Thu Aug 4, 7 pm, Cherry Hill

intro: A Calgary singer and songwriter, between bluegrass and country.
story: Bella White is a Calgary singer and songwriter whose records sit between bluegrass and country: Just Like Leaving in 2020, then Among Other Things on Rounder in 2023. She played Pickathon in 2022 and returned in 2024. A Sign in the Weather, also on Rounder, followed in 2026, and she has a headline run in Texas this December and Treefort in 2027.
sets: Sat Aug 6, 4 pm, Grove · Sun Aug 7, 1 pm, Woods

intro: A New York rapper of dense, dark narratives, half of Armand Hammer.
story: billy woods has made records for Backwoodz Studioz since History Will Absolve Me in 2012, and he is one half of Armand Hammer. Aethiopes, produced by Preservation, came out in April 2022, and Rolling Stone put it among the year's best hip-hop albums. He played Pickathon that August, a Friday afternoon set at the Windmill alongside ELUCID. Maps, with Kenny Segal, followed in 2023, and Golliwog in May 2025; in 2026 he toured Japan, Australia, New Zealand and North America.
sets: Fri Aug 5, 1 pm, Windmill

intro: Doug Martsch's guitar band from Boise.
story: Built to Spill is Doug Martsch's band from Boise, on records since Ultimate Alternative Wavers in 1993; Perfect from Now On (1997) and Keep It Like a Secret (1999) came out on Warner Bros. In 2022 they released When the Wind Forgets Your Name, their first album for Sub Pop and their first original record in seven years, with a new lineup. They came back to the farm that August, four years after the first visit, with a Saturday afternoon set alongside chefs from Gather Around Nutrition. The summer of 2025 brought a co-headlining tour with Yo La Tengo, and in 2026 they returned a third time.
sets: Sat Aug 6, 3:30 pm, Curation · Sat Aug 6, 9 pm, Cherry Hill

intro: A New York songwriter of sideways, observant songs.
story: Cassandra Jenkins is a New York singer-songwriter who put out Play Till You Win in 2017 and then An Overview on Phenomenal Nature in 2021, on Ba Da Bing!; that record landed on thirty-five year-end lists. She played Pickathon in 2022. My Light, My Destroyer, on Dead Oceans, followed in 2024 and made fifteen lists, and a companion record, My Light, My Massage Parlor, in 2025.
sets: Thu Aug 4, 5 pm, Cherry Hill · Fri Aug 5, 5 pm, Woods

intro: A Mississippi Hill Country bluesman, grandson of R.L. Burnside.
story: Cedric Burnside is a drummer, guitarist and singer from Mississippi's Hill Country, the grandson of R.L. Burnside. Benton County Relic (2018) was nominated for a Grammy, and he was on the 2019 bill. I Be Trying, on Single Lock Records in 2021, won the Grammy for Best Traditional Blues Album at the April 2022 ceremony, his first win after three nominations and the first for a Hill Country blues artist. He came back to the farm that summer. Hill Country Love, on Provogue in 2024, was nominated for the same award, and in late 2026 he tours with Samantha Fish.
sets: Thu Aug 4, 8 pm, Paddock · Sun Aug 7, 7 pm, Woods

intro: An Omaha rock and roller who records fast and loud.
story: David Nance is an Omaha rock and roller who records a lot: Negative Boogie in 2017, Peaced and Slightly Pulverized on Trouble in Mind in 2018, Staunch Honey in 2020. He played Pickathon in 2019 and again in 2022, the same weekend as Rosali, whose 2024 record Bite Down was made with his band, Mowed Sound. David Nance & Mowed Sound, his first for Third Man, came out in 2024, he came back to the farm in 2025, and in fall 2026 he went out on his first solo acoustic tour in more than a decade with Simon Joyner & The Ghosts.
sets: Thu Aug 4, 11 pm, Cherry Hill · Sat Aug 6, 4 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A Chicago post-punk quartet, angular and quick.
story: Deeper is a Chicago post-punk quartet. Deeper came out on Fire Talk in 2018 and Auto-Pain in 2020. They played Pickathon in 2022, and Careful!, their Sub Pop debut, followed in 2023. They played European stages through spring 2025.
sets: Fri Aug 5, 4 pm, Grove · Sun Aug 7, 7 pm, Galaxy Barn
Sat Aug 6, 5 pm, Woods · Sun Aug 7, 3 pm, Windmill

intro: A New York rapper, one half of Armand Hammer.
story: ELUCID is a New York rapper who has recorded for Backwoodz Studioz since Save Yourself in 2016, and he is one half of Armand Hammer. I Told Bessie, a record for his grandmother, came out in 2022, the year he played Pickathon, a Friday afternoon at the Windmill with billy woods. REVELATOR followed on Fat Possum in 2024 and made thirteen year-end lists. In November 2026 he and woods surprise-released Snakes & Ladders.
sets: Fri Aug 5, 1 pm, Windmill

intro: A Leeds-born multi-instrumentalist and producer, jazz run through funk.
story: Emma-Jean Thackray is a Leeds-born multi-instrumentalist, composer, producer and vocalist whose jazz runs through funk and chant. Yellow, her first album, came out in 2021 on Movementt and made six year-end lists. She played Pickathon in 2022. Weirdo, on Brownswood and Parlophone in April 2025, was shortlisted for the Mercury Prize, and in 2026 she played a Miles Davis tribute in London and Bristol.
sets: Fri Aug 5, late night (1 am), Cherry Hill · Sat Aug 6, 9 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: A Los Angeles garage-punk band, led by Laena Myers.
story: FEELS is a Los Angeles garage-punk band led by Laena Myers. Post Earth came out on Wichita in 2019, and Subversive Reaction in 2021. They played Pickathon in 2022. Since then Myers has worked on solo music and on string sessions for other records.
sets: Sat Aug 6, 1 pm, Windmill · Sun Aug 7, 1 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: An Atlanta songwriter of pedal steel, R&B and dry humor.
story: Faye Webster is an Atlanta singer-songwriter who signed to Secretly Canadian in 2018. Atlanta Millionaires Club (2019) made eighteen year-end lists and I Know I'm Funny haha (2021) twenty-two. She played Pickathon in 2022, a Saturday-night set at the Paddock and a Sunday-night one in the Woods. Underdressed at the Symphony came out in March 2024, named for the Atlanta Symphony concerts she drifts into, and in October 2025 she played with that orchestra at the Woodruff Arts Center. A summer 2026 headline tour covered North America and the UK.
sets: Sat Aug 6, 10 pm, Paddock · Sun Aug 7, 9 pm, Woods

intro: A Lafayette band keeping Cajun music alive since 1999.
story: Feufollet is a Lafayette, Louisiana band that has played Cajun music since 1999. Their album En Couleurs was nominated for a Grammy. They played Pickathon in 2022, and in 2026 current and former members gathered for a retrospective set at the Louisiana Cajun-Zydeco Fest.
sets: Fri Aug 5, 9 pm, Woods · Sat Aug 6, late night (1 am), Galaxy Barn

intro: Early American fiddle, banjo and song, played as a duo.
story: Frank Fairfield is a Los Angeles fiddler and banjo player who collects 78 rpm records and plays early American songs; he played Pickathon in 2009 and 2010. In 2022 he came with Meredith Axelrod, and the two played folk and jug-band styles together. Since then Axelrod has played folk festivals on her own, and Fairfield has kept to his 78s and to gut-string violin projects in Los Angeles.
sets: Sat Aug 6, 2 pm, Lucky Barn · Sun Aug 7, 5 pm, Cherry Hill

intro: A Los Angeles psychedelic rock band, loud and quick.
story: Frankie and the Witch Fingers is a Los Angeles psychedelic rock band, together since 2013. They played Pickathon in 2022, and in June 2025 they put out the studio album Trash Classic.
sets: Fri Aug 5, 11 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sat Aug 6, 2 pm, Grove

Liquid Swords, on Geffen in 1995, is his best-known solo record, and Beneath the Surface, Legend of the Liquid Sword, Grandmasters and Pro Tools followed. He played Pickathon in 2022 with a live band, the Phunky Nomads, on a Friday night at Cherry Hill and a Saturday evening at the Paddock. Black Samson, the Bastard Swordsman came out in 2025, and he spent 2025 and 2026 on the road with Wu-Tang Clan's Final Chamber tour.
sets: Fri Aug 5, 11 pm, Cherry Hill · Sat Aug 6, 8 pm, Paddock

intro: A Nashville songwriter of plain, moving Americana.
story: Gabe Lee is a Nashville songwriter of plain-spoken Americana, whose The Hometown Kid came out in 2022 and Drink the River on Torrez in 2023. He played Pickathon in 2022, and in 2026 he worked the Southeast and the Pacific Northwest with listening-room and theater shows.
sets: Sat Aug 6, 7 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 7, 4 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A New Jersey jam band that stretches songs out.
story: Garcia Peoples is a New Jersey jam-rock band. One Step Behind (2019) got an Uncut review that likened it to a world rather than an album, and Nightcap at Wits' End followed in 2020. They played Pickathon in 2022, the year Dodging Dues came out on No Quarter. They slowed down their touring afterward, then played Brooklyn's Union Pool in early 2026 with new songs.
sets: Sat Aug 6, 5 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 7, 4 pm, Grove

intro: Griff Washburn, who writes songs aboard a sailboat.
story: Goth Babe is Griff Washburn, who lives aboard a sailboat named Lola; his 2024 album, on Mom+Pop, is also called Lola. He played Pickathon in 2022, a Sunday afternoon in the Woods. In fall 2026 he headlined amphitheaters in Los Angeles, Austin and Queens.
sets: Sun Aug 7, 3 pm, Woods

story: Guerilla Toss started in the Boston area in 2011 and has made art punk you can dance to: Gay Disco in 2013 and then a run of records for DFA, from Eraser Stargazer to Twisted Crystal in 2018. Famously Alive, their Sub Pop debut, came out in 2022, the year they played Pickathon. You're Weird Now followed on Sub Pop in September 2025.
sets: Fri Aug 5, 3 pm, Woods · Sat Aug 6, 11 pm, Galaxy Barn

intro: Alynda Segarra's street-level folk songs, in a band.
story: Alynda Segarra has led Hurray for the Riff Raff since 2006, writing folk songs about the street. Life on Earth came out on Nonesuch in February 2022, and that August the band played Pickathon for the second time, six years after the first, on a Friday night in the Woods and a Saturday night at Cherry Hill. The Past Is Still Alive, on Nonesuch in 2024, made PopMatters' list of the year's eighty best albums, and in 2026 Live Forever, their first live album, was recorded in Chicago and released on Nonesuch.
sets: Fri Aug 5, 11 pm, Woods · Sat Aug 6, 11 pm, Cherry Hill

intro: A Southern California indie band with a hypnotic groove.
story: Inner Wave is a Southern California indie band. They played Pickathon in 2022, and in late 2026 they played multi-night theater runs in California and Mexico.
sets: Sat Aug 6, 3 pm, Galaxy Barn · Sun Aug 7, 6 pm, Grove

story: Jackstraw is a Portland bluegrass band, playing since 1994, with a honky-tonk edge. They have played Pickathon more times than almost anyone, and their 2022 set was the seventh. They still play Portland stages and the Portland FolkMusic Society's shows.
sets: Thu Aug 4, 9 pm, Galaxy Barn · Fri Aug 5, 6 pm, Lucky Barn

intro: A North Carolina guitarist and folklorist of old songs.

Good and Green Again came out in 2022, the year he played Pickathon. When I'm Called, on Fat Possum, followed in 2024, and The Old Beloved Path in September 2026. He toured it that fall with Dougie Poole.

In between came Kassi Valazza Knows Nothing, on Fluff & Gravy in 2023. From Newman Street, in May 2025 on Loose and Fluff & Gravy, was half written at her home on that Portland street and half after she moved to New Orleans; Mojo said her music had miraculously elevated.

She played Pickathon in 2022, a set that began after midnight in the Paddock. I Killed Your Dog followed in 2023 and made twenty-one lists, and fata morgana in August 2026, followed by a fall tour of North America.
sets: Thu Aug 4, late night (12 am), Paddock · Fri Aug 5, 6 pm, Grove

intro: Hannah Read's tender indie rock from Texas.

She played Pickathon in 2022. In 2025 Thx came back as a vinyl reissue, and in late 2026 she headlined club shows in New York.

Valley of Heart's Delight, on Fluff & Gravy and Loose in 2023, was a striking successor in Uncut's words, and Little White Cross arrived in October 2026, with a fall tour through California.

His self-titled album came out in 2022 on Wick Records, the year he played Pickathon. He has since engineered records at his own home studio and played select festivals, among them Field of Vision in Buena Vista, Colorado.

In January 2024 they changed their name to Silverada, and put out a self-titled album that June; Living Proof, recorded at Sonic Ranch in West Texas, arrived in August 2026.

story: MØTRIK is a Portland psychedelic band. They recorded a session for Pickathon's Edge series in 2022 and played the farm the next year.

A deluxe edition of Live-Action came out in early 2026, and he has played the North Sea Jazz Festival in Rotterdam.

intro: A London saxophonist and composer.

She played Pickathon in 2022. Desert Queen arrived in 2025, and in late 2026 she toured the American West, with dates in Idaho and California.

Dancing While Falling, on [PIAS] in 2023, has an Andreya Triana vocal on the closing number, and in 2026 he headlined club and festival nights in Paris and Manchester.

Common Nation of Sorrow, on Signature Sounds, came out in 2023, Kissing Other ppl in 2025, and the single The Long Game in 2026.

She played Pickathon in 2022, the same weekend as David Nance, whose band, Mowed Sound, backs her on Bite Down, her 2024 album on Merge, which made twelve year-end lists. She returned to the farm in 2025, the month before she released Slow Pain: Live and Solo from Drop of Sun.

In September 2023 the Americana Music Association named her Emerging Act of the Year, and Tyler Childers recorded her song Space and Time. Her June 2025 album Planting by the Signs was nominated for Album of the Year and Song of the Year, for Snapping Turtle, at the 2026 Americana Awards.

She toured North America in the spring of 2022 and played Pickathon that August, a Saturday set after midnight at the Paddock and a Sunday-night one in the Woods. Nu Zamrock came out on Loma Vista in October 2026, after a fall tour of American theaters.

In June 2022 they announced that they would break up after that summer's tour, and they played Pickathon that August, a Friday set after midnight at the Paddock and a Sunday-night one at Cherry Hill. The group has been quiet since, apart from catalog uploads in 2026.

They played Pickathon that August, and in late 2026 they were still working US clubs.

story: Sweeping Promises is a post-punk duo, Kansas by way of Boston. Hunger for a Way Out came out on Feel It in 2020, and Good Living Is Coming for You, on Feel It and Sub Pop, in 2023, which made twelve year-end lists. They played Pickathon in 2022. You Say I Romanticize, on Sub Pop, arrived in 2026, and a fall North American tour followed.

intro: A Seattle old-time string band.

They came back in 2022 and again in 2023. Since then they took more IBMA awards and a first Bluegrass Unlimited chart-topper, with Wanderers Like Me, and in late 2026 they opened their 2026-2027 season in Cooperstown, New York.

Their self-titled debut came out in 2022, the year they played Pickathon, a Saturday evening at Cherry Hill and a Sunday set after midnight at the Paddock. Got a Story to Tell, on Penrose and Daptone, followed in 2024, and they played the North Sea Jazz Festival in July 2025.

intro: A West Tennessee songwriter with a voice all her own.
story: Valerie June grew up in West Tennessee, and her 2013 breakthrough, Pushin' Against a Stone, brought a 2014 nomination for the Americana Association's Emerging Act of the Year, the year she was first on the bill. The Moon and Stars: Prescriptions for Dreamers, on Fantasy in March 2021, made twelve year-end lists and was nominated for Americana's Album of the Year; Call Me a Fool, with Carla Thomas, was nominated for the Grammy for Best American Roots Song at the 64th Grammys in April 2022, her first nomination. Ward, came out on Concord in April 2025.

intro: A British duo from the Isle of Wight, deadpan and loud.

Moisturizer, their second album, came out in July 2025.

Acadia, on Nonesuch in October 2024, made six year-end lists, and Allison de Groot and Tatiana Hargreaves, who played the farm in 2023, are on it.
